title: Build VS Code extension to replace deprecated Pieces extension (LTM event injection)
description:
The Pieces VS Code extension was deprecated and has been uninstalled. It was the primary source of structured workstream events feeding PiecesOS LTM — injecting file_open, file_close, tab_switch, copy, check_in, and IDE context (file path, language, line number) into the WPE pipeline on every interaction.

Without it, PiecesOS LTM captures zero IDE context. We need a replacement extension that injects the same events (and more) via the PiecesOS local API.

## Context
PiecesOS exposes a local HTTP API at a dynamic port (currently ~39312). The extension needs to discover this port via lsof or candidate probing, then POST SeededWorkstreamIngestion objects to /workstream_pattern_engine/ingestions/create as events occur.

Application IDs:
- VS Code Insiders app ID: 24e066ee-81aa-4054-ba7a-74697135b086
- OS_SERVER app ID: B960C645-A6CC-4654-932C-C38EBA6F54A6

Known event types from WorkstreamEventTrigger model:
- file_open, file_close (on editor open/close)
- tab_open, tab_close, tab_enter, tab_leave, tab_switch (on tab changes)  
- application_enter, application_leave (on VS Code focus/blur)
- check_in (periodic heartbeat every ~60s when VS Code is in foreground)
- copy (on clipboard write from editor)
- url_changed (if webview/browser panel is used)

Context carried per event:
- WorkstreamEventContext.ide: { file path, language ID, line number, column, git branch, repo name }
- WorkstreamEventContext.native_clipboard: { copied text (for copy events) }
- readable: human-readable string e.g. 'Editing src/index.ts in openclaw'

Additional events NOT in original extension (opportunity):
- Git events: branch switch, commit, merge, push (via git extension API)
- Terminal events: command run in integrated terminal (with working dir + exit code)
- Debug events: breakpoint hit, debug session start/stop
- Extension activation: language server start/stop
- Search events: workspace search queries and result counts
- Diff view: file comparisons opened
- Claude Code activity: session start/end (via file watcher on ~/.claude/projects/)
acceptance_criteria:
Extension publishes to VS Code Marketplace (or installable via VSIX)
Injects all WorkstreamEventTrigger event types on correct triggers
Carries full IDE context per event (file, language, line, repo, branch)
Discovers PiecesOS port dynamically (no hardcoded port)
Gracefully handles PiecesOS being down (queues or drops, no crashes)
Emits check_in heartbeat every 60s when VS Code has focus
Registers correct Application object matching the original VS Code app ID
notes: Gap analysis showed the original extension was injecting thousands of events per day. During the 9-day outage (May 26 - Jun 4 2026), we lost all IDE context from ~10,793 Claude Code user turns across 28 repos. A reconstruction script will inject synthetic events from Claude Code transcripts + git log + Screen Time data to backfill the gap.

title: syndicate: commitPartialProgress swallows original sync error if the recovery commit itself throws
description: cli.ts's runSyncArticles wraps the per-article loop: on a sync failure it tries to commit whatever changedFiles accumulated so far (commitPartialProgress), then rethrows the original wrapped error. But if commitAndPush itself throws during that recovery commit (push conflict, network blip, git lock), the original sync error is completely discarded -- not chained as .cause, not logged. The operator sees only the git failure with zero indication a specific article's sync also failed underneath it. Narrow (requires two independent failures in the same run) but a genuine double-fault swallow on the safety-critical commit path. Found during final holistic review's verification of the partial-commit-loss fix. Fix: wrap the recovery commitAndPush call so if it throws, the resulting error chains/mentions both the original sync failure and the recovery-commit failure.
notes: Not blocking merge; filed as deferred follow-up per final review.

title: syndicate: commitAndPush([]) silently falls back to committing everything staged
description: git.ts's commitAndPush now scopes commits via 'git commit -m msg -- ...paths', but git commit -m msg -- (bare trailing -- with zero paths) is NOT equivalent to an empty pathspec that commits nothing -- git treats it as no pathspec given and falls back to committing all staged content, silently reintroducing the exact bug just fixed in Task 12. Both current call sites (runSync guards on changedFiles.length===0 before calling; runBaseline always passes [filePath]) are safe today, but the function itself has no guard. Add an early-return/throw for paths.length===0, or at minimum a doc comment noting the precondition. Found during Task 12 final code quality review.
notes: Not blocking Task 12 merge; filed as deferred follow-up per code review.

title: syndicate: isArticleOnWebsite scans whole document, not scoped to writing-list
description: src/website-status.ts's isArticleOnWebsite() checks html.includes(href="${articleUrl}") against the entire site/index.html document, not scoped to the writing-list container. If the canonical URL is ever referenced elsewhere on the page (canonical <link>, OG tags, footer, share widget), this returns a false positive, computeGaps treats website as already synced, and insertWritingCard is never called -- the article silently never gets its writing-card entry even though frontmatter says synced. description:
## Why

Agents (and humans) entering this repo have no quick orientation to what projects exist and what they do. A single reference table — project name, one-line summary, key entry points, and an 'agent can learn more at' pointer — would let any LLM or contributor get oriented in seconds.

## What needs to happen

1. Enumerate all projects: top-level directories and nursery/* subprojects (currently: claude-switcher, obsidian-user-base, openclaw-setup, orb-autostop, pieces-babysitter, pieces-metrics, site, installer).
2. For each project, gather: name, brief purpose summary, primary language/stack, status (active/incubating/stable), and where an agent should look to learn more (README path, CLAUDE.md section, skill file, etc.).
3. Decide on the best delivery format:
   - A sub-doc linked from the global CLAUDE.md (e.g. docs/PROJECTS.md)
   - A superpowers skill that surfaces the table on demand
   - Or both (doc as source of truth, skill as loader)
4. Write the table and wire it up so agents automatically get it loaded.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every project in the repo has an entry
- Each entry has: name, one-line description, stack, status, agent-entry-point
- The table is reachable from CLAUDE.md (direct link or via skill)
- An agent starting a new session can answer 'what projects are in this repo?' without reading code
acceptance_criteria: Every project has an entry; table linked from CLAUDE.md; new-session agent orientation works

title: Build agentic-repos catalog skill for global CLAUDE.md injection
description:
The joe-stack-preferences skill already has references/agentic-repos.md with a table of all Joe's repos. The goal is to make Claude reach for the right tool proactively without being told.

## Problem

Claude currently only knows about agentic repos if joe-stack-preferences is invoked. That skill is triggered by stack/architecture questions — not by general task requests that happen to touch a repo that already exists.

## Work Items

1. Evaluate whether agentic-repos.md inside joe-stack-preferences is sufficient or if a standalone skill makes more sense for discoverability.
2. If standalone: create `~/.claude/skills/agentic-repos/SKILL.md` that activates when someone mentions building something that already exists in Joe's ecosystem (PR reviewer, MCP server, marketplace plugin, etc).
3. Add a `### Agentic Repos` activation entry to global CLAUDE.md under `## Skills activations` so Claude auto-invokes it when the task domain matches one of these repos.
4. Define the trigger criteria clearly: what phrases / task types should activate this skill?
5. Keep the catalog current as new repos are created — consider a convention for adding new entries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Claude, starting a fresh session with no prior context, suggests using an existing repo rather than building from scratch when the task clearly matches one.
- The skill activation is low-noise: it does not fire on every coding task, only when there is a plausible repo match.

title: Add tests for claude-switcher (claude-use.zsh)
description:
claude-use.zsh now has meaningful functionality (launchctl setenv, JSONC inline comment stripping, profile switching, status output, clear command) but zero tests. Add a test suite to verify all major behaviors so future changes can be made confidently.

Test coverage needed:
- _cu_persist_launchctl: sets vars via launchctl setenv, clears via unsetenv
- _cu_persist_vscode_env: JSONC stripping preserves string literals containing //, trailing comma removal, correct JSON output
- cu status: shows launchctl state (vertex / oauth token / none)
- cu clear: clears shell env AND launchctl vars
- Profile loading: vertex profile sets VERTEX keys, clears OAuth; OAuth profile sets token, clears VERTEX keys
- Array subscript fix: _cu_env[] works without quotes

title: syndicate: insertWritingCard's marker string is uncommented, coupled to site/index.html's exact tag form
description: src/website-publisher.ts's insertWritingCard locates the insertion point via indexOf('<div class="writing-list">'). This works today but any future hand-edit to site/index.html that adds an attribute to that div (e.g. an id) would make the whole function throw, aborting the entire sync run rather than gracefully skipping just the website platform. Add a one-line comment noting the coupling, and/or consider a more robust marker match. Found during Task 6 code quality review.
